```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# --- Load ---
# Use the full file, not penguins_clean.csv, which only kept two measurements
penguins = pd.read_csv("data/penguins.csv")

measurements = {
    "bill_length_mm": "Bill Length (mm)",
    "bill_depth_mm": "Bill Depth (mm)",
    "flipper_length_mm": "Flipper Length (mm)",
    "body_mass_g": "Body Mass (g)",
}

# --- Process ---
penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(subset=list(measurements))

summary = (
    penguins_clean
    .groupby("species")[list(measurements)]
    .agg(["mean", "std", "count"])
)
print(summary.round(1))

# --- Plot: one panel per measurement, one bar per species ---
species = summary.index
colors = ["#F8766D", "#00BA38", "#619CFF"]   # same default colours as ggplot

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 8))

for ax, (col, label) in zip(axes.flat, measurements.items()):
    means = summary[(col, "mean")]
    sds = summary[(col, "std")]
    bars = ax.bar(species, means, yerr=sds, capsize=5, color=colors, alpha=0.85)
    ax.bar_label(bars, fmt="%.1f", padding=3, label_type="center", color="white")
    ax.set_title(label)
    ax.set_ylabel(label)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

fig.suptitle("Mean Penguin Measurements by Species (± 1 SD)", fontsize=14)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("data/penguin_measurements_by_species.png", dpi=300)
plt.show()
```
